papers.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
papers.label: arXiv:2611.27113v1

summary.one_liner: The paper gives a new proof of the "n! theorem" for rational Cherednik algebras, using their representation theory together with an analogue of rotating complex structures coming from a quaternion action.
summary.plain: This paper is about a known result in algebra, the "n! theorem," which concerns the symmetric group of permutations of n objects and a family of structures called Cherednik algebras. The author gives a new proof of this result rather than announcing a new finding. The proof combines the study of how these algebras act on vector spaces with a mathematical trick that resembles rotating a complex structure, driven by an action of the quaternions.
summary.why: The text is short, so it is unclear exactly which parts of the n! theorem are reproved or how much the new route simplifies earlier arguments. Its value likely lies in offering an alternative proof that links representation theory with quaternion-based ideas, but the abstract alone does not show how far that connection extends.
summary.background:
- Representation theory: studying abstract algebraic objects by how they act on vector spaces, often as matrices.
- Symmetric group: the group of all rearrangements of n objects; its size is n!.
- Cherednik algebras: a family of noncommutative algebras that generalise objects tied to symmetric groups and reflection groups.
- Quaternions: an extension of complex numbers with three imaginary units, forming a non-commutative number system.
- Complex structure: a way of treating a real vector space as a complex one, via multiplication by i; "rotation" here is an analogy for changing such structures.
- The n! theorem: a result about the dimension or count of certain representations, tied to n!; the text does not state its exact form.

papers.abstract: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

papers.title: The weighted fundamental lemma for non-split groups
papers.label: arXiv:2611.26750v1

summary.one_liner: The paper proves the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general quasi-split unramified groups, adapting the Chaudouard–Laumon geometric proof from the split case, and deduces Waldspurger's nonstandard version and a twisted version used to complete Moeglin–Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted trace formula.
summary.plain: This is a paper in pure mathematics about symmetry groups and the counting identities that link them, which underpin the study of how number-theoretic objects are organized. The author extends a known geometric proof, originally worked out for "split" groups, to a broader class of groups called quasi-split groups. The text reports that this yields an identity between certain adelic orbital integrals, which is the central claim, along with consequences for automorphic theory.
summary.why: The text claims the work makes certain results unconditional, including the endoscopic classification for classical groups and several downstream consequences. Whether these claims hold is for specialists to assess; the summary here relies only on the authors' stated implications.
summary.background:
- Representation theory: the study of symmetry groups through how they act on vector spaces.
- Reductive group and Lie algebra: a continuous symmetry group and its linearized version.
- Quasi-split and unramified groups: special classes of groups over local number fields with a controlled structure.
- Orbital integrals and trace formula: averages over group elements that feed into counting formulas linking automorphic forms.
- Fundamental lemma: a identity comparing orbital integrals across related groups, a key tool in the Langlands program.
- Higgs bundles and Hitchin base: geometric objects on a curve used as a tool in the proof.
- Deligne–Mumford stack: a generalized geometric space that allows symmetries of its points.

papers.abstract: In this work, we prove the Weighted Fundamental Lemma for Lie algebras for general (quasi-split) unramified $G$. The strategy is to adapt the proof of Chaudouard--Laumon from the split case. In particular, we define the notion of a $\xi$-stable Higgs bundle for a quasi-split reductive group scheme $G$ on a curve, and prove that the stack of such form a proper, finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over the Hitchin base when $G$ has anisotropic center. We then adapt the global cohomological theorem of Chaudouard--Laumon to the quasi-split setting, and perform the required Frobenius-point count to obtain an identity of adelic orbital integrals. A local-to-global argument deduces the WFL for Lie algebras. In the last chapter, we perform a parallel reduction to deduce Waldspurger's nonstandard WFL from a global version which follows from the same geometric theory. Our work implies the Twisted Weighted Fundamental Lemma in good characteristic, which completes Moeglin--Waldspurger's stabilization of the twisted Arthur--Selberg trace formula. We therefore render unconditional the endoscopic classification for classical groups and an array of downstream consequences in automorphic theory.

papers.title: On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
papers.label: arXiv:2611.25676v1

summary.background:
- Hopf algebra: an algebraic object that generalizes symmetry groups, with a way to multiply and to split elements.
- Quasi-triangular: carries an extra structure (an R-matrix) that gives a consistent way to swap tensor factors, which is the "braiding."
- Semisimple: decomposes cleanly into simple building blocks, with no tricky nilpotent parts.
- Cocommutative: the splitting operation does not depend on the order of factors, which is the signature of a group.
- Tensor category and fiber functor: a category of representations with a way to multiply objects; a fiber functor identifies it with vector spaces, which is what makes it a group's representations.
- Frobenius–Perron dimension: a generalized notion of size for such categories.
- Square-free: an integer not divisible by any square greater than 1 (e.g. 6, 30 but not 12).
summary.one_liner: The paper proves that a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra over the complex numbers whose dimension is square-free is semisimple and cocommutative, and hence that a corresponding braided finite tensor category with a fiber functor comes from a finite group.
summary.plain: This is a pure-mathematics note about a family of algebraic structures that describe symmetries, specifically those whose size (dimension) is not divisible by any perfect square other than 1. The author shows that, for these structures, a certain "braided" refinement collapses to the simplest case: the structure behaves like the symmetries of an ordinary finite group. The text itself is short and gives only the main statement, not the detailed argument.
summary.why: It strengthens the classification picture for finite tensor categories by showing that a extra braiding condition forces a square-free-dimensional case to be group-like. Its broader significance is unclear from the abstract alone, and I have not checked how it relates to other classification results.

papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.

papers.title: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
papers.label: arXiv:2611.26505v1

summary.background:
- Lie algebra: a mathematical structure describing continuous symmetries, such as rotations.
- Lie superalgebra: a generalization where some components are "odd" and anticommute, used in physics for supersymmetry.
- Quantum group: a deformed version of a symmetry structure, depending on a parameter q, often at a root of unity.
- Divided powers: a way of building integral forms (versions defined over the integers) of algebras, avoiding division.
- PBW basis: a Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt basis, an ordered set of building blocks spanning the algebra.
- Root system and Weyl groupoid: combinatorial data encoding symmetries of a Lie-type structure.
- Nichols algebra: a graded algebra arising from braided vector spaces, used to build quantum groups.
- Frobenius morphism: a map in characteristic-type settings whose kernel and cokernel are smaller, simpler pieces of the structure.
summary.one_liner: The paper constructs super analogues of Lusztig's quantum groups of divided powers, with PBW-type bases indexed by super-type root systems, Lusztig isomorphisms realizing the Weyl groupoid, and a Frobenius-type morphism relating a small quantum group (a Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra) and the enveloping algebra of a semisimple Lie algebra.
summary.plain: This is a piece of abstract algebra about "quantum" versions of symmetry structures, the kind that describe how systems can be transformed while keeping track of their internal rules. The authors build a new family of such structures that behaves like objects built from "super" symmetries, which mix ordinary and sign-flipping (odd) components. They show these objects have organized bases and symmetry-like maps, and they relate them to a smaller finite version and to a classical Lie algebra via a Frobenius-type map.
summary.why: The work extends Lusztig's divided-power quantum groups, a central framework in representation theory, to the super setting, where the usual Lie-algebra tools need modification. The connections it draws between finite-dimensional quantum objects and classical Lie algebras are the kind of link that matters in this area, but the text alone does not show how far these results reach beyond the authors' framework.

papers.abstract: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

papers.title: Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras
papers.label: arXiv:2611.24139v1

summary.background:
- Vertex operator superalgebra: a graded algebraic structure with both even and odd (fermion-like) parts, used to describe two-dimensional conformal field theory.
- Weight: the grading by scaling dimension; weight-1, weight-3/2 and weight-2 pieces are the generators studied here.
- Strong generation: the whole structure is built from the given low-weight pieces.
- Quasi-primary: a vector annihilated by the lowest-order part of the symmetry action, used to project out unwanted terms.
- Lie superalgebra: a Lie algebra extended with odd elements.
- Lie–Rinehart algebra: a pairing of a Lie algebra acting on a commutative algebra by derivations.
- Commutative associative algebra, idempotent, Artinian: standard algebra notions; an idempotent decomposition splits the algebra into orthogonal pieces.
- Universal object and simple quotient: the largest structure with given generators, and its irreducible version.
summary.one_liner: The paper classifies and constructs vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by weight-1, weight-3/2 and weight-2 subspaces, using two canonical commutative algebras inside the weight-2 part and a Lie–Rinehart-type quadruple that encodes compatibility conditions for an associated Lie superalgebra.
summary.plain: This paper is about a family of algebraic structures that behave like symmetry systems in physics: they are built from pieces graded by "weight" (a measure of how the pieces scale). The authors show how the rules among the building pieces can be packed into a single four-part object, and they use it to construct a family of these structures and describe their simple versions. They also state that when one of the key algebras is finite-dimensional, it splits into a tensor product of simpler pieces.
summary.why: The work offers a general framework that the authors say includes known examples such as superconformal algebras and generalized BMS_3 (super)algebras, which is why it may matter to people working on conformal field theory and related symmetry algebras. The text does not show wider applications, so its reach beyond this algebraic setting is uncertain.

papers.abstract: This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace. We demonstrate that the algebraic structures of the generating subspaces are encoded by a quadruple that generalizes Lie--Rinehart algebras and their weak representations. This quadruple yields necessary and sufficient compatibility conditions for constructing an associated Lie superalgebra $\mathcal{L}(\mathfrak{g},A,U)$. Based on this, we construct a family of universal vertex operator superalgebras $V_{\mathcal{L}}(\ell,0)$ and establish a reconstruction theorem for their simple quotients under certain conditions. If $A$ is finite-dimensional, we prove that its orthogonal idempotent decomposition into local Artinian summands naturally induces a tensor product isomorphism of the corresponding vertex operator superalgebras. In addition, our general construction encompasses many vertex operator superalgebras, such as superconformal algebras and generalized $\mathrm{BMS}_3$ (super)algebras.

papers.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
papers.label: arXiv:2611.24471v1

summary.background:
- Category: a collection of objects and maps between them, used to organise algebraic structures.
- Abelian category: a category that behaves like modules over a ring, with kernels and cokernels.
- Exact sequence: a chain of maps where the image of each map equals the kernel of the next; exact functors preserve these.
- Tensor (symmetric monoidal) category: a category with a compatible notion of multiplying objects together.
- Field k and characteristic p: the number system base; positive characteristic means arithmetic wraps around modulo p.
- Tannakian category: a tensor category that arises as representations of a group.
- Balmer spectrum: a topological space built from a tensor triangulated category, used to classify its ideals.
- Frobenius functor: a functor tied to raising elements to the p-th power in characteristic p.
summary.one_liner: The paper introduces semi-exact functors between abelian categories, shows they are exact for a canonical exact structure, and uses them to define a support theory for symmetric tensor categories that is conjectured to match the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when the category is finite.
summary.plain: This work is about the abstract algebra of "categories" (collections of mathematical objects and the structure-preserving maps between them). The authors study a class of maps called semi-exact functors, which either preserve or break exact sequences, a kind of chain of objects that is neatly balanced. They show such maps always behave well with respect to a suitably chosen notion of exactness, and they use them to build a way of assigning "support" to symmetric tensor categories.
summary.why: The support theory is meant to match an existing invariant, the Balmer spectrum, which organises the structure of tensor triangulated categories, so the work links two frameworks. The authors state the main matching is only conjectured and proved in a weak form and in special cases (Tannakian categories and characteristic 0), so its full scope is not yet settled.

papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

papers.title: Algebraic Vector Fields on Compact Homogeneous Spaces are 2-generated
papers.label: arXiv:2611.22265v1

summary.background:
- Manifold: a smooth curved space that locally looks like ordinary Euclidean space (e.g., a sphere).
- Compact Lie group: a continuous symmetry group that is closed and bounded, such as rotations of a sphere.
- Transitive action: the group can move any point of the space to any other point.
- Vector field: an assignment of a direction and speed at each point, generating a flow of motions.
- Lie algebra: the linear-algebra structure that encodes infinitesimal symmetries of a group; "generated by two elements" means every element is obtained from two by brackets and linear combinations.
- Diffeomorphism group: all smooth reversible reshapings of the manifold; its identity component is the part connected to doing nothing.
- Dense subgroup: a set whose elements can get arbitrarily close to any element of the target.
summary.one_liner: For a compact connected manifold with a transitive action of a compact Lie group K, the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields is shown to be generated by two vector fields, so the flows of these two generate a dense subgroup of the identity component of the diffeomorphism group, with explicit generators for spheres obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.
summary.plain: This paper studies smooth "flows" that move every point of a closed, curved shape (a manifold such as a sphere) in a continuous way. It considers a special family of such motions, the "algebraic" vector fields, which behave nicely under a symmetry group acting on the shape. The main result is that this whole family can be built from just two basic motions, and that repeatedly applying those two motions can get arbitrarily close to any smooth deformation of the shape that can be reached continuously from doing nothing.
summary.why: It gives a compact description of a large family of motions on symmetric spaces using only two generators, which is a structural statement of interest in Lie theory and differential geometry. The text does not show further applications, so its wider relevance beyond this area is unclear.

papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact, connected manifold on which a compact Lie group $K$ acts smoothly and transitively. We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields on $M$, i.e., of smooth vector fields whose translates under $K$ span finite-dimensional spaces, is generated by two vector fields. Consequently, the subgroup generated by the flows of these two vector fields is dense in the identity component of the diffeomorphism group of $M$. For spheres, explicit generators are obtained from earlier results on spherical vector fields.

papers.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
papers.label: arXiv:2611.23377v1

summary.background:
- Lie algebra: a mathematical structure describing continuous symmetries; sl_2 is the simplest nontrivial case.
- Poisson structure and deformation quantization: a classical way of describing a system's observables, and a systematic way of turning it into a quantum version controlled by a small parameter (here ħ).
- W-algebra: an algebra of symmetry-type observables that generalizes the Virasoro algebra of two-dimensional conformal field theory.
- Affine current algebra and level k: the basic symmetry algebra of a chiral theory, with a number k that labels its strength; the abstract states a shift of this level by the dual Coxeter number h^∨ times ħ.
- Chern–Simons theory and 3D gravity: topological and gauge-theoretic models in three dimensions; chiral gravity is a specific proposed gravity theory.
- Boundary conditions (oper and Dirichlet): rules for how fields behave at the edge of the space.
- Perturbative quantum equivalence and 1-loop exactness: agreement of two quantum theories order by order in a small expansion parameter.
summary.one_liner: The paper builds explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine W-algebras for every simple Lie algebra, using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model, and proves a perturbative quantum equivalence between sl_2 Chern–Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity.
summary.plain: The paper concerns a family of algebraic structures (affine W-algebras) that arise as the boundary observables of a physics model living in three dimensions. The authors construct "quantum" versions of these structures, meaning versions where the quantities no longer commute in the naive way, using a specific field-theory framework. For the simplest case, sl_2, they argue that two physical descriptions, Chern–Simons theory and chiral gravity, agree at the quantum level and state how their parameters relate.
summary.why: It links quantization of W-algebras, which are central objects in representation theory and conformal field theory, to a concrete three-dimensional physical model. The text does not show wider consequences beyond these constructions, so the broader significance is uncertain from the abstract alone.

papers.abstract: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng. A linear differential-graded presentation identifies the universal bulk with Chern--Simons theory near a principal nilpotent background, where holomorphic gauge gives a finite, 1-loop exact quantization. The quantum oper boundary observables form the principal affine $W$-algebra at level $k-h^\vee\hbar$; we also obtain this level shift directly for affine current algebras. For $\mathfrak{sl}_2$, we prove a perturbative quantum equivalence between Chern--Simons theory and three-dimensional chiral gravity, including their oper and Dirichlet boundary conditions, and determine the quantum relation between their parameters.

papers.title: Two categorifications of the Kekulé relations
papers.label: arXiv:2611.20184v1

summary.background:
- Representation theory and algebra: relations are equations that a structure must satisfy.
- Categorification: replacing a number-level identity with a richer structure (such as a category) whose "shadow" recovers the original identity.
- Foam evaluation: a way of assigning values to decorated surfaces ("foams") used in knot homology, with a kernel of relations that evaluate to zero.
- Kekulé relations: algebraic relations introduced by Morrison; the abstract gives no further detail on them.
- The abstract is brief, so full definitions and proofs are not visible here.
summary.one_liner: The paper finds new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation and uses them to categorify all the Kekulé relations introduced by Morrison, plus an equivalent family of relations that also receives categorifications.
summary.plain: This is a research-level paper in algebra about a family of algebraic rules (called Kekulé relations) that were proposed by Morrison. The authors show how to lift these rules from simple numerical identities to richer structures built from geometric "foams," which is the sense of "categorification." They also find an equivalent set of rules and give categorifications for those as well.
summary.why: Categorification tends to link algebraic invariants to deeper structures, and foam evaluations are part of that framework, so the work is of interest to specialists in knot and link homology. The short abstract does not show what the categorifications are used for beyond this, so any wider connection is unclear from the text alone.

papers.abstract: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelulé relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.

papers.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
papers.label: arXiv:2611.20659v1

summary.background:
- Affine vertex algebra: an infinite-dimensional algebraic structure from conformal field theory, built from a Lie algebra and a level (a number parameter).
- Admissible level: a special, non-generic value of that parameter where the representation theory is well-behaved.
- Zhu's C_2-algebra: a commutative, finite-dimensional quotient of a vertex algebra that captures its leading structure.
- Jacobian ring: the quotient of polynomials by the partial derivatives of a potential function; it measures how degenerate the function's critical points are.
- Chevalley isomorphism: a standard identification between invariant polynomials on a Lie algebra and on its Cartan subalgebra (a maximal commutative subalgebra).
- Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction and Slodowy slices: a procedure that reduces a symmetry algebra to a smaller one, and a transverse slice to a nilpotent orbit used to model that reduction.
- Simply-laced vs non-simply-laced: whether a Lie algebra's root system has all roots of equal length; Dunkl equations are a generalization of ordinary differential equations suited to unequal root lengths.
summary.one_liner: The paper proves a conjecture of Kang, Lawrie and Song that the C_2-algebra (Zhu's finite-dimensional quotient) of simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebras is a Jacobian ring of an invariant potential built from a polynomial twisted period, and extends the description to non-simply-laced principal cases.
summary.plain: This paper is about a precise algebraic dictionary between two kinds of mathematical objects that arise in the study of symmetries of quantum field theories. The authors show that a certain finite-dimensional algebra attached to a family of such symmetry structures matches exactly the algebra of a polynomial "potential" function, which was conjectured earlier by Kang, Lawrie and Song. They also check that the same matching holds for related reduction constructions, and they extend the result to a class of cases where the underlying root structure is not simply-laced.
summary.why: Matching a conjectured identity to a proof is useful for specialists because it ties vertex algebra theory to singularity theory via Jacobian rings and Slodowy slices. The text does not discuss wider applications, so any further connections should be treated as speculative.

papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with root-length-dependent multiplicities.
